newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges Germany to wait on repatriating Bosnians.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges Germany to wait on repatriating Bosnians.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday it is too soon to forcibly return some Bosnian refugees to parts of their homeland where they would be in the ethnic minority.

"The United States strongly supports the voluntary return of refugees and displaced persons to Bosnia," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said at a briefing. "We do believe that it is premature to return forcibly Bosnians to areas where their ethnic group is in the minority."

Burns urged Germany to work closely with the United Nations on repatriation of refugees "to differentiate, to distinguish, between Bosnians from areas where their ethnic group is in the minority and those from areas where their ethnic group is in the majority."
Burns cited recent repression by Croatians against minority Serbs in the Krajina region and violence in eastern Slavonia as evidence that conditions were not yet ripe for a return of all refugees.

There are still some 300,000 Bosnian refugees in Germany, most of them Moslems driven out of areas now ruled by Serbs, and cash-strapped German officials are increasingly determined that they should go back to Bosnia soon.
Burns noted that Germany had taken in more Bosnian refugees than any other country, and commended their humanitarian behaviour since 1992.
Burns said the United States expects to admit up to 18,000 refugees from the former Yugoslavia, primarily Bosnians, by the end of September, and has admitted over 38,000 Bosnian refugees since 1992.
